1549: Sweet William, snapdragon, larkspur, Canterbury bells, bluebonnets, cockscomb; thyme and white clover made themselves at home among their herbaceous cousins, and the low growing plants, aubretias, veronica, sedum, saxifrage, sweet pinks, and fuchsias, in bold masses, ran in and out, as if playing hide and seek with their lusty neighbours, and hurrying forward joyously, outdistanced them, even invading the path in their eagerness to be seen.

The cactus had nearly done blooming now, and its ever listening ears were absurdly waited with fruit; gorgeous carpets of bluebonnets were spread beside the ditches, while the air above was filled with thousands of yellow butterflies, like whirling, wind blown petals of the prickly pear blossom.
They were one with the bluebonnets that flecked the sweep of the divides with royal colour; one with the mourning dove whose love cry sounded from the alders fringing Teapot.
